analysis_steps.goal: Obtain Halpha and stellar kinematics from PHANGS-MUSE

method.value: Use PHANGS-MUSE copt mosaics; Halpha flux and kinematics from pPXF with Halpha fitted as an additional Gaussian while the stellar continuum is fitted simultaneously

key_parameters.value: seeing of the copt data 0.96 to 1.25 arcsec

assumptions.value: Halpha and Hbeta velocity and velocity dispersion tied together

evidence.quote: The velocity and velocity dispersion for H$\alpha$ and H$\beta$ are tied together.

analysis_steps.goal: Model galaxy rotation of the Halpha velocity field

method.value: 3D tilted-ring fit to the Halpha datacube with 3D-BAROLO; PA, inclination and centre fixed to literature values

evidence.quote: In order to model the galaxy rotation, we utilize ((cite: diteodoro_15)) which is a tool for fitting 3D tilted-ring models to emission-line datacubes.
The position angle, inclination of the galaxies, and center are fixed to the values from Table 2 of (cite: lang_20) in running 3D–BAROLO.

key_parameters.value: velocity dispersion fixed to 8 km/s, scale height fixed to 0 arcsec

evidence.quote: Velocity dispersion and scale height of the disk are fixed to 8 km$\,\rm s^{-1}$ and 0 arcsec, respectively

key_parameters.value: PA and inclination either fixed or free ring by ring; both results presented in the velocity-jump analysis

evidence.quote: In fitting galaxy kinematics using 3D–BAROLO, position angles and inclinations can be fixed or freely modeled ring by ring.

validation.value: Rotation model is not used for the final gradient maps because non-smooth models give bumpy gradient maps; stellar velocity used instead

evidence.quote: However, when galaxy rotation models are not smooth, the resulting velocity gradient maps becomes bumpy and thus unsuitable for investigating the velocity gradients.

method.value: Take the Halpha-minus-stellar (or Halpha-minus-rotation-model) velocity map, rotate it to align the bar horizontally, take 1-pixel differences left/right and up/down and add the horizontal and vertical gradients in quadrature

evidence.quote: We rotate the velocity residual map to align the bar horizontally using the position angle of the bar presented in Table 1
We move along the velocity residual map by 1 pixel (0.2”, 11 $\sim$ 19 pc depending on object) to the left ($V_{\rm res,-1pix}$) and to the right ($V_{\rm res,+1pix}$)
We add in quadrature both the horizontal ($\nabla V_{x}$) and vertical ($\nabla V_{y}$) velocity gradients to obtain the full velocity gradient.

claims.hypothesis: Bar-driven shocks and shear produce enhanced velocity gradients along the bar dust lanes
claims.experiment: Halpha velocity gradient maps from V_Halpha - V_star (PHANGS-MUSE) for four barred galaxies
claims.result: Enhanced velocity gradients along the dust lanes, covering almost the whole bar except for NGC 1365
claims.finding: Velocity gradients are enhanced where shocks and shear are expected

evidence.loc: 3.3 Velocity gradients due to bar-driven gas inflow
evidence.quote: Enhanced velocity gradients clearly show up along the bar dust lanes and they extend out for a considerable length, almost covering the whole bar except for NGC 1365.

claims.hypothesis: Large velocity jumps occur across the high-gradient regions even without circular rotation
claims.experiment: Pseudo slits across high-gradient regions in Halpha and PHANGS-ALMA CO velocity maps, with and without rotation-model subtraction
claims.result: Halpha and CO velocities jump by up to ~170 km/s after rotation removal and deprojection (50 to 150 km/s range in summary)
claims.finding: Bar-driven shear and shocks produce velocity jumps comparable to earlier observations and simulations

evidence.quote: find that H$\alpha$ and CO velocities jump up to $\sim$ 170 km$\,\rm s^{-1}$, even after removing the effects of circular motions due to the galaxy rotation.

claims.hypothesis: Star formation is inhibited where bar-driven shear and shocks are strong
claims.experiment: Compare extinction-corrected Halpha SFR surface density with velocity gradient per spaxel (coloured by Sigma_mol from CO) and compare BPT SF fractions in high versus low gradient bar regions
claims.result: Upper envelope of SFR surface density decreases with velocity gradient; fraction of SF spaxels is lower in high-gradient bar regions
claims.finding: SF is inhibited in the high velocity gradient regions of the bar

evidence.quote: find that star formation is inhibited in the high velocity gradient regions of the bar, and the majority of those regions are classified as LINER or composite

claims.hypothesis: Emission-line ratios are elevated toward composite or LINER by bar-driven shear and shocks
claims.experiment: BPT classification of spaxels in high versus low velocity gradient bar regions
claims.result: Most high-gradient regions are composite or LINER; difference negligible for NGC 1512
claims.finding: Elevation may be due to shocks, but absence of recent SF revealing LINER-like emission cannot be ruled out

evidence.quote: But we cannot rule out that the absence of recent SF results in revealing LINER-like emission-line.

limitations_admitted.value: Velocity gradients are lower limits because of spatial and spectral smoothing

evidence.loc: 3.3 Velocity gradients due to bar-driven gas inflow
evidence.quote: Our results should be considered as a lower limit of the velocity gradient because of the smoothing effect due to the spatial resolution

limitations_admitted.value: Perpendicular or parallel gradients do not cleanly separate shear from shock because dust lanes are curved

evidence.quote: Thus, even velocity gradients perpendicular (parallel) to the bar may not perfectly represent shear (shock).

limitations_admitted.value: Direct comparison of velocity jumps with simulations is not straightforward because only line-of-sight velocity is measured

evidence.quote: It is not straightforward to directly compare the values of velocity jump from simulations with our observational data analysis, because we only measure the line of sight velocity.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only four galaxies; the SF-inhibition conclusion rests on a qualitative envelope in SFR surface density versus gradient plots with no stated statistical test
High-gradient threshold (upper 5th percentile per galaxy) is relative, so each galaxy always has an H region regardless of absolute shear
Halpha-based SFR in LINER/composite regions can be contaminated by non-SF ionisation, which is circular with the BPT-based SF fraction
SFR relation printed with 5.3 x 10^42 (likely sign typo in exponent) and no stated uncertainty
ALMA CO provides only context and Sigma_mol colouring; CO velocity gradients not obtainable over the whole bar so the shock/shear signal is entirely Halpha-based
Masking constant C chosen empirically per galaxy (0.2 vs -0.05) may influence the gradient maps

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Small to moderate: PHANGS-MUSE mosaic cubes (several GB each) plus PHANGS-ALMA CO moment maps for four galaxies; no raw ALMA visibility processing needed
reproducibility.score_reason: Public PHANGS data products and a fairly explicit gradient-map recipe with numeric thresholds, but pseudo slits, BAROLO ring settings, bar radius definitions and PHANGS-ALMA product details are missing and no code is released.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: ALMA plays a minor supporting role and the main Halpha/BPT results depend on MUSE products and several undefined region and slit choices.
